text:
Guillaume Brisebois is the kind of depth defenseman every team needs in November: a 2015 third-round pick who has spent most of his career in the AHL and gets the call when injuries hit. With Tom Willander out, he has played five games for Vancouver, about 15 minutes a night, with one assist.

Five games is far too few to judge, and we'll say that plainly. The early numbers aren't kind, the Canucks have taken 29% of the expected goals with him on the ice, but on a team losing most nights, a depth defenseman's on-ice numbers mostly reflect who he's out there with.

Before this season he had 30 NHL games, with one goal and two assists. Our range has a huge spread for a full season, 9 to 29 points, which really means we don't know and neither does anyone else. His job is simpler: keep it simple, get the puck to the forwards, and hold the spot until the regulars are back. When Willander returns, Brisebois likely goes back to waiting for the next call.
headline: Brisebois holds the spot
